드워프가 산의 뼈라고 부르는 돌입니다. 쪼개면 푸른 쇠의 결이 드러나고,: Dwarves call it the bones of the mountain. Split it and blue veins of iron show; set it in a wall and it becomes the wall, hammer it into a blade and it becomes the blade. Dwarves grow talkative at the sight of ore — almost the only time dwarves ever do.
북쪽 끝 얼음 궁전에서 녹지 않고 내려온 왕관입니다. 쓰는 순간 머리카락: A crown that came down unmelted from the ice palace of the far north. The moment it is worn, frost blooms from the tips of the hair, and what leaves the fingertips is no longer light but a spear. The crown does not choose its bearer. It simply does not come off a head easily once worn.
무덤 아래 왕국을 다스리던 군주의 관입니다. 쓰면 귀가 밝아져 땅속 망자: The crown of a lord who ruled the kingdom beneath the graves. Wear it and your ears sharpen to the whispers of the dead underground, and every dawn someone presses something into your hand. The witch still can't tell whether they are loyal or merely bored.
그동안 마녀가 외운 주문을 몰래 다 받아 적어 둔 책입니다. 펼치는 순간: A book that secretly copied down every spell the witch ever recited. Open it and it spews them all out at once. Whether fire or ice comes out is up to the book, but luckily the book likes the Lodge too.
화로 안에 사는 늙은 불의 정령은 걷지도, 칼을 들지도 않습니다. 그저: The old fire spirit living in the brazier neither walks nor lifts a blade. When night falls it simply stretches and lobs fireballs at the forest one by one. It needs no firewood. It does need a little praise.
겨울이 끝날 때 한 번만 울린다는 낡은 청동 종입니다. 종소리가 닿는 곳: An old bronze bell said to ring only once, when winter ends. Everything its toll reaches collapses like an avalanche, and a strangely quiet morning follows. The witch's grandmother rang it twice, they say, but never told the story of the second time.
